title: 2020-01-10 Meeting notes - User management GitHub & Azure DevOps
content:
Meeting Date: 2020-01-10 09:00

Location: Microsoft Teams Meeting + Malmö Central - 2nd floor - 204

Link to Outlook Item: click here

Invitation Message

Updated invite sent from my new account and additional persons added per request from Jathisan.


Agenda:

Round the table introductions

Rationale for CI/CD pipeline user handling

Describe desired functionality

Discuss possible solutions and timeline


Background Information:

We have started our pilot (DEXF) project for CI/CD based on GitHub and Azure Pipelines. Already the pilot project make it evident that we need resolve how we should handle users in an efficient way. DEXF has 20 repositories, this times number of users that need to be added to each repository will create a lot of administration and of course risk of users not being removed from all repositories when they leave project. For roll-out to all other IPEX projects this will not work.

Preferably the user handling should be via the AD and automated as much as possible. However I think that we still need to have the possibility to add users in manual way in case of users joining a project that do not have an IKEA account.


Desired functionality:

  • User that is added/removed to AD is automatically added/removed to GitHub
  • Github Teams are synchronized with AD
  • All users should have read access to all IPEX repositories
  • Possible for IPEX admin to invite users that do not have an IKEA account
  • Manage GitHub Apps
  • Distribute management of teams to the projects
  • MFA enabled
  • SSO



Possible solutions:

Use the Teams function in GitHub Cloud Enterprise. Currently as an organizational member I can invite external users as collaborators to a specific repository but this does not scale. When I read pages

https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/about-organizations

https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/adding-organization-members-to-a-team

it seems that we can solve this either by letting e.g. two persons in IPEX become owners in the inter-IKEA organization or we could add a new GitHub organization for IPEX where persons for IPEX are owners.


Use internal repositories to support visibility and collaboration.

https://help.github.com/en/github/creating-cloning-and-archiving-repositories/creating-an-internal-repository


At least in the beginning we would need to be able to add external users to be able to mitigate long on boarding to IKEA accounts.

If we use the automatic sync as described on this page

https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/synchronizing-teams-between-your-identity-provider-and-github

We could perhaps have automatic sync of all IKEA domain accounts and then have specific teams for external uses so that handling would be somewhat easier?



Use GitHub Owner and team maintainer permissions to distribute user management.

Organization owners:

  • Invite non-members to join a team and the organization.
  • Manage GitHub Apps
  • Remove members when they get AD account


Team maintainers:

  • Add organizational members to teams


https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/inviting-users-to-join-your-organization

&

https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/permission-levels-for-an-organization


You can connect up to five IdP groups to a GitHub team, and an IdP group can be assigned to multiple GitHub teams without restriction.

Parent teams cannot synchronize with IdP groups, but are used by Team maintainers to assign access to repositories.


https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/synchronizing-teams-between-your-identity-provider-and-github

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/saas-apps/github-tutorial

Members of child teams also receive notifications when the parent team is @mentioned, simplifying communication with multiple groups of people.

https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/about-teams

Requiring two-factor authentication in your organization, should be done from scratch

https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/requiring-two-factor-authentication-in-your-organization
